correctness.rationale: The exact two Lloyd maps are defined on short circular Voronoi arcs. Uniform-density Jacobian is J0=I/2+(S+S^{-1})/4; the reflection-odd restriction removes its only unit multiplier. The analytic implicit-function theorem gives the unique local pinned branches, and continuity yields attraction on that invariant subspace. Differentiating the integrals gives both displayed all-n first-order coefficients. f(L)=L^2+L sin L cos L-2sin^2 L has f(0)=f'(0)=0 and f''(L)=4sin L(sin L-L cos L)>0 on (0,π/3], proving the strict coefficient inequality. Exact difference of the von Mises weights about a cell center yields the negative sine-angle drift for all positive κ. The standalone numerical checker reproduces representative finite cases; no infinite statement relies on it. Important limits: no full-space attraction or global optimality.

value.rationale: The problem is forced by a current stability analysis at a regular von Mises codebook and an earlier comparison of geodesic versus chordal Lloyd quantizers. The result replaces a nonfixed symmetric configuration by rigorous reflection-pinned branches; it gives explicit finite-n first-order behavior for both objectives and a strict model-dependent separation, together with an all-positive-concentration obstruction to uniform polygons. This is a structural stability-and-quantization gap, not a sampled numerical improvement. Scope is limited to local reflection-symmetric attraction; further global dynamics are not asserted.
